# Real-Time Object Detection (WebGPU)

> Free, open-source web app that detects and tracks objects in a webcam feed or a video file in real time, entirely inside the browser. It uses YOLO26 and YOLOE models running on the device's GPU through WebGPU and ONNX Runtime Web. Nothing is uploaded: no server, no account, no install.

- Live app: [webgpu-object-detection.vercel.app](https://webgpu-object-detection.vercel.app/)
- Source code: [github.com/CodeRafay/realtime-object-detection](https://github.com/CodeRafay/realtime-object-detection)
- Author: [Rafay Adeel](https://github.com/CodeRafay)
- License: Apache-2.0 (app code); model weights by Ultralytics are AGPL-3.0

## Features

- Webcam or uploaded video file as input
- Three quality modes:
  - Fast: YOLO26n, 80 everyday COCO object classes
  - Accurate: YOLO26s, 80 COCO classes, about 25% more accurate than Fast
  - More objects: YOLOE-26s open-vocabulary model, 268 classes including smartwatch, glasses, earbuds, keys and wallet
- Object tracking (ByteTrack-style): every object gets a stable ID and boxes move smoothly with it between model frames
- Adjustable minimum-confidence slider
- Runs on WebGPU, with a WebAssembly fallback for browsers without WebGPU
- Privacy: camera and video frames never leave the device

## Measured performance

Accuracy (mAP50-95) on 500 COCO val2017 images none of the models were trained on; speed on an Intel UHD 620 laptop integrated GPU in Chrome with WebGPU:

- Fast (YOLO26n): mAP 0.380, 7-8 model frames per second, 5 MB download
- Accurate (YOLO26s): mAP 0.475, about 2 model frames per second, 19 MB
- More objects (YOLOE-26s): mAP 0.370, about 2 model frames per second, 21 MB
- Boxes are redrawn at the display rate (about 60 FPS) between model frames

## Requirements

A recent Chromium browser (Chrome or Edge 113+) for WebGPU. Firefox and Safari run on the slower WebAssembly fallback. Camera access requires HTTPS.
